column4: zero cargo-deny violations: the allowlist and every named ban, over the phase that finally spent the dependency budget — forty-eight packages join the lockfile across P4, 238 to 286, jsonrpsee's server half bringing hyper into the graph at P4b, which is what turned N5's wire-crate wall from hypothetical into live (note N38), and N57's declined dependency paid at P4f for the generated subscription client. G3's row could say "over a phase that added no dependency"; this one cannot, so the licenses arm reads forty-eight manifests it has never read and the bans arm holds over a graph wide enough to hide a door — deny.toml is the authoritative population and every entry carries its own reason

every shipped gate predicate green over the tree, the P4 additions included — and the row that makes this gate's predicate population derived rather than transcribed, because run-all.sh walks scripts/gates/ rather than a list. Twenty-two predicates run and ten of them are named by no g4 row at all, the load-bearing one being counted-selections.sh: it proves that no `tests` row of this very table has silently gone to zero, which is v1's "`just gate-g4` counted" and note N10's whole family — the defect class of a gate that stayed green while checking less than it claimed. A criterion reachable only through this row is a criterion G4 could not close without it. The G4 review's agents-md-current.sh — the deployed AGENTS.md against docs/10, the drift the file's own opening anticipates and nothing checked — is the tenth, and it stays unnamed deliberately: docs/7 commissioned no criterion for it and it proves nothing P4 built, so a g4 row of its own would claim a phase asked for it. It arrives through this row, and through the identical row at g0, g1, g2 and g3, which is the right reach for an invariant that has held since the v2 series was issued at f6bc5d9 rather than since P4

state writes still go through webcam-handler-engine::store::write_json_atomic now that the thing writing them is a daemon holding the state directory for its whole lifetime (D9) — with the raw-write population docs/9 widened at P4e-i, which is what this row exists to run: the pattern was std's spellings only until daemon::server::open_destination taught this workspace another one, opening through rustix and turning the descriptor into a std::fs::File as note N51's discharge, so it now also matches the write-shaped OFlags and deliberately not rustix::fs::open( itself, which SocketDir uses O_PATH | O_DIRECTORY while naming XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. The third instance of note N10's family — a state write spelled a way the gate's hand list had never seen — and a widening commissioned for G4 that no g4 row named

the unsafe boundary's three claims, the third of them P4d's and never named by a phase row at any letter (design §2.5, rubric B10 [V] and B11): the token appears only inside the V4L2 backend's src/sys/; every crate root outside it carries #![forbid(unsafe_code)], with one root added since G3 — the client library P4f landed, in the population the moment it became a workspace member; and the residual-unsafe register in that module's mod.rs, the counted table of one row per block and the sentence above it that states the totals, describes the tree it is in. P4d is what made the third claim load-bearing rather than decorative: it put a kernel-facing module (sys::uevent) inside the exempt region and added no register row, because rustix is a safe wrapper, and "the count below is unchanged by it" was a sentence a reader had no way to check — the next edge written with libc would have made it quietly false

the --json answers still validate against the committed JSON Schema bundle, with the verb population still scraped from wch --help at both levels and an exact row match. P4 added no verb to wch, which is why this row is not the repetition it looks like: P4f gave cli_core's clap tree two consumers and made the binary's name a parameter of the parse (note N64), so a verb added for wchc's sake lands in wch's help too and fails here without a validation row, and a tree that grew a per-root identity is a tree whose help output the scrape has to keep reading. It is also what anchors cli-parity.sh: that gate proves wch and wchc answer byte-identically, and byte-identical to something unvalidated is two binaries agreeing without either of them being right (design §2.7, docs/7 P4f)

no camera frame reached the tree over the phase that taught this project to write a photo from a process nobody is watching (rubric A12): D10's ServerPath sink lands a file on the daemon's host at a path the client names, a calibrate sweep driven over a socket writes one sample photo per sample into a session tree wchd owns, and binary(signals) parks a subprocess wchd on a fifo at the second sample's own photo path. Three ways for an image to be created by a wchd rather than by a test, so the predicate's content check — every file in the tree sniffed for a magic number, extensions and .gitignore being advisory rather than privacy controls, corpus/images/ the one place an image may live and only under its three conditions — is answering a question G2's and G3's rows could not ask

the one piece of transport code we own, version-coupled to jsonrpsee 0.26 and integration-tested on both sides: a real client's JSON-RPC call and its answer crossing a real Unix socket, every bound the socket runs under driven rather than declared (batch size, request body, an answer past jsonrpsee's own default, and connections held past the cap), the WebSocket half of the same socket **upgraded** now that this build bounds it — the assertion P4b made inverted rather than deleted, and the handshake asserted to have been agreed to rather than merely answered 101, which is what a client would otherwise hang on (note N57), a give-up on accept reported as a failure rather than a clean stop, and D11's socket directory held as a descriptor rather than checked as a name — created 0700, a wider one refused rather than repaired, a symlinked one refused inside the openat itself however private its target — as ENOTDIR, because under O_PATH it is O_DIRECTORY that refuses a link and O_NOFOLLOW that leaves one to refuse, measured rather than assumed — one owned by another uid refused in both directions, one re-permissioned between the check and the bind refused and one substituted between them *defeated* rather than detected (the socket lands in the inode whose mode and owner were asserted, and a checked directory that was unlinked fails the bind closed), a socket left by a dead daemon replaced only because D9's lifetime lock says no daemon is alive — the replacement reached by a real client connecting by D11's own name — and both spellings of the bind driven, the /proc/self/fd one a host with procfs gets and the by-name fallback it cannot otherwise reach, the second serving a real client and announcing itself at WARN so the downgrade N39 allows can never be silent (D11, notes N38 and N39)

read-verb integration tests over the in-memory and UDS transports: list, info, controls, get, calibrate status and calibrate list driven through the generated T5 client on both wires, every answer compared to the one engine or backend call behind it, and the two wires proven to be two rather than one run twice

the mutating half of the wire surface that writes to a camera or to a process, over both transports: set in both guard directions with the automation switch-off written first and named, a driver clamp arriving as a warning with {requested, applied} intact rather than as a refusal, snapshot/restore with an owned control counting as restored, discover_pairs writing to the camera and the device itself asserted back where it was found, profile_capture, photo over both of D10's sinks — a verbatim camera JPEG compared byte for byte against the engine's own after base64 and a socket, a file landing on the daemon's host and the answer saying where, the negotiated size surfaced when it differs from the request, a relative server path, an extension this build cannot write and a fifo or directory named as a destination all refused before any camera opens with the camera still answering afterwards, an empty camera id refused rather than resolving to the only camera on the host, and two photos in flight sharing one descriptor rather than streaming twice — and terminate_holder driven for real: a pid that does not hold the node refused HolderGone with nothing signalled, a child process this suite forked signalled and its exit status asserted to be a signal, a holder past the walk's reporting cap still nameable and signallable while the ones the caller did not name are left alive, the answer naming the target back, still_held answered rather than rendered as an error, and no other verb signalling anything when it meets Busy — with every refusal these verbs can make recovered client-side through api::codes::typed: Busy staying Busy, a settle timeout never arriving as a device that vanished, and StoreLocked never reachable (AGENTS rules 5, 7 and 8, design §5, D12, E6, notes N9, N34, N35, N42, N46 and N48)

the eight calibrate_* verbs over the wire (D8, D9): a session opened, planned, reordered, swept, selected, applied and restored over a socket and compared against engine::lifecycle reading the same state directory, the D8 refusals each verb can make — a second session in one slot, a queue order that is not a permutation, a control this camera does not have, apply before the queue is settled — the fingerprint check walked across all six mutating verbs and the read one, naming the fields that differ rather than being implemented once out of seven, each verb resolving its camera exactly once so the session's fingerprint and the device the writes reach are one reading of the machine, calibrate restore consuming the pre-sweep snapshot and being run twice without an error, plan --order proven to open no camera, no verb answering StoreLocked, and a queue edit proven unable to interleave with a sweep rewriting the same session — which flock cannot prevent inside one process (rubric B5, notes N14, N20, N23, N43 and N47)

the T5 surface is mounted whole and routed whole: the pinned routing list is api::METHODS itself, derived-against rather than transcribed, so a twentieth method cannot land unrouted and unremarked and the surface has no unrouted half left for a "not built yet" refusal to inhabit — the map note N43 inventoried is gone and P4d deleted the variant it answered with, which makes that absence structural rather than checked (note N6 retires here), and the registration a real into_rpc() produces is asserted to be that same pinned surface, which is what joins this claim to the method-count walk's; plus the three things the daemon adds on top of an engine call, each in both directions — a photo sink refused before a camera opens — relative, an encoding this build cannot write, and a destination that is not a regular file, the last of which is now asked of the descriptor an O_NONBLOCK open returns rather than of the name, so a fifo answers ENXIO instead of parking a camera's actor thread in open(2) forever and no client can step between the check and the write (note N51's discharge) — a photo answer checked against itself before it is sent, the bounded holder re-check answering in both directions on a paused clock and costing the number of walks its constant states, and terminate_holder's diagnosis: a camera with no capture node and a request naming this daemon (D10, design §5, notes N6, N34, N43, N46, N48 and N51)

the T5 method-count walk (docs/9 Part 2, note N28): every method the daemon's own into_rpc() registers is exercised over the fake and answers, on both transports — the exercised side recorded at the transport from the generated client's own spelling rather than listed beside it, so a wire method with no test stops the count — the one assertion that carries the row, proven red by deleting a call and pinned non-vacuous against the nineteen crates/api pins rather than by a loop that could not fail; one non-vacuous assertion per answer, which the compiler requires for every method because an answer nobody reads is dead code; the registered set **partitioned** rather than filtered by hand now that four of its names belong to two subscriptions no ClientT can send — the unsubscribe half derived from api::SUBSCRIPTIONS and asserted to be a subset before it is subtracted, so removing a name nothing registered weakens nothing silently, and both counts pinned: nineteen calls, and nineteen plus two per subscription registered (notes N29 and N57); and the recorder itself asserted to write down what crossed the wire and nothing else, refusals included

the two things the daemon says without being asked, over both transports (D10, docs/7 P4e-i): every subscription the daemon's own registration carries driven to a real delivery — a hotplug event off the daemon's own watch thread and a progress event out of a real sweep, decoded from frames that crossed a real WebSocket on the daemon's own AF_UNIX socket — with the population walked from api::SUBSCRIPTIONS so a subscription with no delivery test stops the walk rather than passing in silence, watched red by adding a third row to wire_surface! and seeing the walk name it; one upgraded connection carrying a subscription and a call at the same time, which is the duplex fact P4f's client transport has to be built against rather than discover, with the plain HTTP transport beside it unaffected; a subscriber that stops reading costing counted drops and never the daemon — the bound read from limits::WS_MESSAGE_BUFFER_CAPACITY rather than transcribed, the split between the two hops asserted exactly because both instants are signals rather than guesses (the reading subscriber taking the last event says the producer finished, the daemon's own loss count reaching the overflow says the stalled subscriber's task did), a second subscriber on the same source losing nothing, and the daemon still answering three refusals that discriminate while the slow one is stuck — watched red against a hand-applied send().await, which becomes a named nextest TIMEOUT rather than a hang; disconnect mid-sweep, both halves docs/7 names and rubric B6 spells — the sweep continues to a document engine::lifecycle reads back through the same function calibrate_status answers from, the subscription is reaped, and the server then stops, which is what a leaked bridging task would turn into a TIMEOUT; events emitted with nobody subscribed dropped and counted, both directions, so the same sweep with a subscriber attached adds nothing to the count; the per-connection subscription bound refused as a -32006 answer to the subscribe call before any handler runs, with a second connection unaffected by the first one's refusal; the two lag policies as a fold with both arms and the typed count a hotplug close carries, which is the one decision no fixture can force; the fake's watch corrected to honour the deadline its trait declares — woken by a Condvar a scripted fault ends, so a test never waits out a duration and the daemon's watch loop is not a spin; the message buffer a *real* connection gives a subscription read back off its own sink and asserted to be the number this project chose rather than jsonrpsee's default, which no in-memory dispatch can say because there the buffer is an argument (rubric A8, note N59), with the in-memory arm reporting the different number it was handed so the field is an observation and not a second copy of limits; the hotplug watch's own two failure directions, both of them reachable only because the fake's exhaustive fault menu grew the variants for them — a host that cannot give a watch out refusing the subscribe call with a D13 code before the accept, which is the one moment a subscription can still carry one and the whole reason the watch is started lazily, and a watch that stops under an open subscription ending that subscriber's stream with a named reason rather than leaving it accepted, counted and silently blind for the life of the process (rubric A4, note N59) — watched red against an arm that only cleared its flag, which becomes a named TIMEOUT because that is what a stranded subscriber looks like from outside; the watch thread's own lifecycle, started by the first subscriber and put down after the last one leaves and taken up again by the next, which is the one thing limits::HOTPLUG_WATCH_DEADLINE_MS participates in — no fault is scripted after the last unsubscribe on purpose, so the thread's turn comes from that deadline and from nothing else, and an hour-long one is a named TIMEOUT (measured); a client that floods one WebSocket connection with waiting captures behind a camera a sweep is provably holding, bounded at limits::CAMERA_ENQUEUE_WAITERS permits and refused past it with the same Busy the flag already promises — the bound this transport removed and note N56 wrongly claimed the connection count still supplied, watched red at 36 parked where 32 is the bound; and the hostile directions a client can take, one test apiece and every one of them closing with the same question — a client that subscribes to everything this daemon offers and then vanishes, whose slots come back and whose watch a second client can still use; a session named at subscribe time proven not to be a filter, because the wire carries no such parameter and a client that believed it had one would drop other sessions' events unknowingly, with the session-shaped refusal where it belongs, on the sweep, and the stream neither closed nor fed a phantom event by it; one client watching one sweep twice, told twice under two ids on one connection; a subscription outliving the session it watched and carrying the next one's failure as an event whose discriminant is the one its caller was refused with, because a terminal event is terminal for a control and never for a stream; a whole D8 arc — sweep, select, apply, restore — ending under a watcher and ending only the session; and a connection that dies in the middle of a message with unread notifications past its buffer still in flight — each of them then asking the daemon a verb it must answer over the connection that did the damage and over a fresh one, plus the plain POST the upgrade shares a listener with, because a wedged daemon fails to return rather than failing an assertion; nothing here sleeping, every wait ending when the subject speaks (notes N17, N28, N29, N38, N49, N53, N57 and N59)

one declaration, two generated traits, two inventories, and no hand list on either side (D10, notes N28 and N57): the whole T5 surface's registration read off a real RpcModule — both into_rpc() calls merged the way the daemon merges them, which is the only place a name colliding across the two halves can be caught — and compared against METHODS unioned with every name SUBSCRIPTIONS carries, twenty-three because jsonrpsee registers an unsubscribe callback beside every subscription (N29's accounting: the registered population grows by four while D10's method count grows by two), the two halves asserted disjoint so every consumer may partition rather than filter, every wire spelling pinned by name including the two unsubscribe ones jsonrpsee derives rather than we, each subscription carrying a summary that is a sentence, an # Errors section and an item type a document can name, and the precondition both unsubscribe derivations share — a name beginning subscribe — asserted rather than trusted, since the two agreeing is only true because of it; and the OpenRPC document emitting methods as exactly the call surface while the subscriptions are an x-subscriptions extension carrying both wire names, the notification name and the item schema, asserted in both directions because a subscription described as a method would promise a call the HTTP half of this socket answers -32603 and would say nothing about the payload, which is the only interesting part of it

D12's per-camera actor threads: nothing opens until a verb needs the device, an idle camera's descriptor is closed by the driver the daemon spawns — the spawned task, on its own cadence, with no test asking for a pass — one wedged camera never holds that pass for the others, a thread that dies stops claiming the descriptor it dropped, and a command that ran longer than the timeout is not closed by the pass that follows it while a shorter one still is (note N45's discharge, both directions); every deadline driven by the now_ms its caller supplies and every cadence by a paused clock, so nothing here sleeps (notes N41, N42 and N45)

D12's wait flag and the bound it needs (notes N42 and N51, discharged together because they are one mechanism): a camera's command queue refuses a caller that will not wait and one whose deadline has already arrived with the same Error::Busy and the same empty holder list, so the flag chooses when the answer arrives and never what it says; a caller that does wait is admitted when the running command frees a place — observed, not guessed, because the actor's one thread is provably held and the waiter says so before this test lets go — and one whose thread dies while it waits is told DeviceGone rather than Busy (E3); the wait budget read from limits::CAMERA_ENQUEUE_WAIT_MS in exactly one place and asserted in both directions, and the number of callers that may hold that budget at once bounded by limits::CAMERA_ENQUEUE_WAITERS and driven past it — the bound the WebSocket surface removed from the transport, since one connection can hold arbitrarily many calls in flight and every waiter parks a blocking-pool thread the whole daemon shares (note N59); the flag itself asserted both ways where the daemon reads it and both ways across the wire, at a camera whose queue is provably full — proven by reading exactly the refusals a flood of twice the seats must produce — so the two spellings get D12's two different answers at one instant rather than the same answer twice, which is what a wire test that could not tell them apart looked like and why the daemon ignoring the field entirely is now a red run at workspace scope; and note N51's race closed at the same time — a photo's destination resolved once, before any camera is touched, by an O_NONBLOCK open plus an fstat on the descriptor, so a fifo is a refusal rather than a parked thread, a directory and a missing parent stay distinct refusals, an existing file is not truncated before the bytes exist, and a client that renames the checked file away mid-capture finds the photo in the inode this daemon approved rather than in the fifo it put in its place; nothing here sleeps — every wait ends when the subject speaks, and the deadlines are bounds nothing reaches

hostile-bytes fixtures for the netlink parser — the malformed and truncated halves of docs/7 P4d's row, because a packet off a kernel socket is attacker-shaped input (rubric B10); the flood half is arranged at the socket rather than at the parser and is asserted by the row below, since a file of concatenated packets is one packet and would assert the wrong thing: twelve committed datagrams — five a real kernel broadcast and seven synthetic, because no kernel produces a truncated datagram and the README says which are which — each asserting a different answer, so "malformed" and "a shape this build cannot read" are never spelled the same way (AGENTS rule 6); the R3 hotplug recipe exists and selects tests — one uvcvideo cycle through the blessed helper, with every camera closed and never --force, watched while it happens and seen through the real CameraBackend::watch as removals of nodes that were here followed by arrivals, and the events applied to the pre-cycle node listing proven to reproduce the kernel's own listing afterwards; the helper's absence, an unblessed helper, a camera somebody else holds and an unload that did not take are four different named counted skips rather than one silent pass, and design §3.3 item 9's mid-stream device loss stays the fake's because the interlock makes it unarrangeable here (the run itself is evidence, not CI-gating — note E9)

docs/9's UDS-permissions row: the socket directory a shipped wchd served from is 0700 and owned by the user who ran it, a wchd handed a directory anyone can walk into refuses to serve and does not repair it, and a second uid cannot walk in where the host offers one — a named, counted skip where it does not (D11, note N44)

the order the daemon stops in, driven over its own seams (docs/7 P4e-ii, note N61): SIGTERM and SIGINT producing one identical teardown; the supervisor told STOPPING before a subscription is cancelled and before the socket closes, which is the step that only buys anything if it is first; the transport not stopped until the cancelled subscriptions have actually ended, asserted as the open count at the instant the stop happened rather than as a scheduling hope; a subscription that never ends held to the one deadline the whole teardown shares rather than to a second full-length one; a drain that finishes inside the bound saying nothing and one that runs out of it naming the bound and stopping anyway (AGENTS rule 3: a wait that expires is never a silence); an accept loop that gave up reported rather than swallowed, and that same failure surviving a teardown which could not drain, because a daemon that stopped serving must not exit clean; and the real signal source answering both signals and nothing else — every step recorded as a value by a double, because an order of side-effects that leave the process is only assertable against something that writes them down

the four protocols a service manager speaks, taken apart over values (docs/7 P4e-ii, design §2.6 and D11): a supervisor nobody is running sending nothing, opening nothing and logging nothing, which is what lets main pass the real one unconditionally instead of asking whether this is systemd; the watchdog a task only when $WATCHDOG_USEC says somebody is holding a stopwatch, pinged inside the interval that manager set; an inherited socket adopted only when its directory passes the same check_mode_and_owner the self-bound path uses — refused in a directory anyone can walk into, refused when the address is abstract because there is then no directory, no mode and no owner to authenticate with, refused when more than one descriptor arrives because picking the first would be a guess an operator cannot see — with the startup line naming which of the two paths this daemon is on; the $JOURNAL_STREAM decision made by comparing the device and inode this process's stderr actually has rather than by trusting the variable; and a startup enumeration that failed answered as a STATUS line rather than as a daemon that will not start (E3, AGENTS rule 7)

docs/9's commissioned signal-parity row, against a real process at last (note N61): one test per signal, SIGTERM and SIGINT delivered for real to a wchd that is mid-sweep with a subscription open across it, each producing one eight-field record rather than two lists of assertions that could drift while both stayed green — the ending's reason is events::SHUTTING_DOWN and not a socket that went away, the daemon was alive with work in flight when the signal arrived, the samples the sweep answered with are the samples on disk, the photo's bytes crossed the fifo so the wedge was the sweep rather than the test's idea of it, the exit is zero, the state lock is free, and the socket file is still there because uds.rs argues at length that it is deliberately not unlinked; the sweep is held mid-flight in a process nothing can reach into by a fifo at the second sample's own photo path, derived from the Session the daemon answered with, which works only because calibrate.rs writes sample photos through a blocking std::fs::write and deliberately not N51's non-blocking open (note N62); watched red against a teardown that cancels nothing (both tests TIMEOUT), a stop that does not drain, a daemon that unlinks its socket, SIGINT handled alone, and step 3's wait first removed and then left unbounded

the same protocols against a real subprocess wchd rather than against values (docs/7 P4e-ii): READY=1 arriving on a notify socket this suite binds, before any camera has been walked, with the count of cameras following as a second STATUS that says at startup because nothing keeps it live; a unit that asks for a watchdog pinged inside the interval it set; a daemon with no $NOTIFY_SOCKET serving and saying nothing to anybody, which is the measurement that makes Unsupervised stop being a choice; and a $JOURNAL_STREAM naming a stream that is not this stderr leaving the fmt layer exactly where it was — the half socket-activation.sh completes on a host with a real journal, where the same line's _TRANSPORT is what tells the two layers apart

the shipped unit files say what the daemon needs them to say, every value re-derived from the tree rather than read and nodded at (docs/7 P4e-ii, design D9/D11): Type=notify and never Type=forking and no PIDFile=, because the process a supervisor starts is the process that serves — which is what makes NotifyAccess=main sufficient and D9's lock record name the pid systemd knows; SocketMode=0600 and DirectoryMode=0700, systemd's own default being 0755 and D11 making filesystem permissions the whole authentication model, so this is the half that keeps the daemon's own refusal from ever having to be reached; ListenStream= ending at the socket composed from schema::paths::APP_DIR and schema::limits::DAEMON_SOCKET_FILE, so a rename in either crate turns this red instead of shipping a unit that binds a socket nothing connects to; and TimeoutStopSec exceeding limits::DAEMON_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS, the pair that can only be wrong together — whichever is smaller is the bound that fires, and if it is systemd's then the ordered release never runs and every sentence this project writes about how wchd stops describes a path nothing takes

a real wchd under a real service manager, which is the only place two of these claims can be driven at all (docs/7 P4e-ii, design D11, note N39's amendment): systemd-socket-activate binds the socket and the daemon serves that very socket, compared by inode — read once when the activator says it is listening and again once the daemon says it is serving, so never binds its own is asserted rather than assumed — with the path the daemon announces checked beside it, because binding the right inode and announcing another is a daemon nobody can find; an abstract-namespace address refused outright, since there is then no directory, no mode and no owner to check rather than something this build merely cannot verify; more than one inherited descriptor refused rather than guessed at; and a stderr that really is the journal getting structured entries from the journald layer installed instead of the fmt layer, told apart by _TRANSPORT=journal under a transient systemd-run --user unit. On this host every arm ran for real and no skip was taken, and the named counted skips exist and were exercised green by an arm of their own (note N44's reason for a shell predicate rather than a declining #[test])

the deferrals the tree named in place, discharged where each of them sat (docs/7 P4e-ii, notes N58 and N61): server.rs's idle-sweep driver ending itself on the same token rather than being detached, which is what makes step 6 a join and not a hope about a task nobody waits for; uds.rs's Serving::stopped answering the same question twice, a latent panic found by needing the answer twice — the teardown races that handle against a signal and then awaits it again as the drain, and a JoinHandle polled after it has yielded panics, on the stopping path, in a task nobody joins; and, from the outside over a real socket, a daemon that is stopping ending every open subscription with events::SHUTTING_DOWN in a payload the client can branch on rather than with a connection that closed underneath it, which is step 3 as a client sees it

docs/9's CLI-parity row (docs/7 P4f, design T4/T5/D9): wch and wchc answer one surface, compared as bytes over a real socket and a real fake-backed daemon. The population is the surface's own — leaf verbs scraped from wch --help at both levels with an exact row match, so a verb added without a bucket fails and a row naming a verb the surface dropped fails too — and every leaf lands in one of four named buckets rather than being quietly absent: compared (the six read verbs, byte-identical --json and both exit zero); exempt-session (the six calibrate writes, because comparing them would mean two sessions in two states, and D9 gives a running daemon the store lock for its lifetime so wch cannot write one at all — asserted in LockProtocol::HeldForLifetime's own words, read out of schema::error rather than transcribed); exempt-device (set, restore, photo, profile capture, because wch and wchd each replay the profile into a device state of their own and a comparison would write to two devices); and exempt-stamped (snapshot, which mutates nothing but stamps taken_at with the instant of the read — measured to differ in exactly that one field and no other, so the exemption is proved rather than asserted). terminate_holder is out of the population by construction and not by exemption: it has no T4 spelling (note N48). docs/9's 'local-only verbs, none at P4' is tested rather than repeated — every exempt verb is driven through wchc alone and must answer, and a verb only wch could run would name itself there. The fixture also exercises the property it rests on: one wch reads the very state directory a live wchd holds, because read verbs take no lock under either D9 protocol

the shipped wchc end to end (docs/7 P4f): the refusals it owns without a daemon — a socket nothing is listening on named by path, an unset $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR told apart from it, the two composition-root flags refused by clap's ValueSource before the socket is touched, and clap's exit 2 kept distinct from the daemon's exit 1 — and then the verbs it answers over a real AF_UNIX socket against a real wchd replaying a committed profile: the read verbs, one T4 verb reaching two wire methods and answering the same document, a photo arriving as base64 and as a file on the daemon's disk, a profile captured over the wire, and the whole calibration arc. The sweep's progress is asserted from the events themselves while the call that owns them is still in flight, which is the one property a subprocess could never show — the shipped watcher draws nothing when stderr is not a terminal (measured), which is why the crate has a library at all

the thin client's own decisions, taken apart over values (docs/7 P4f): the socket composed from schema::paths::runtime_dir and schema::limits::DAEMON_SOCKET_FILE — the two homes wchd composes it from, so a fixture cannot pin a path the daemon would not bind — and the refusal that names $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR when there is nowhere to put one; --backend and --profile refused by provenance and not by value, with every other global flag passing, without which the refusal would swallow every command line; the per-verb request timeout, where only calibrate sweep gets the unbounded-by-design budget and the two constants are asserted to differ so the walk is not vacuous; and the sweep's consumer-side event filter both ways, exact by session id and falling back to the swept control under --task (note N57's per-client stream, filtered here)

one command tree, one name per root (docs/7 P4f, design T4, §2.10): cli_core::Program is a closed vocabulary and the name is a parameter of the parse, so --help, --version and the usage block of every clap error carry the right binary's name off the one tree, and {program}: {error} has one home rather than one per consumer. Anchored assertions rather than contains-based, because wch is a prefix of wchc and a substring assertion could never go red; the well-formedness walk debug_asserts once per root, so a tree that is malformed under only one of the two names is still caught. The g1 package(webcam-handler-cli-core) row runs these tests already; it names the clap tree and both renderings, not the per-root identity P4f added, and a criterion nobody named is a criterion nobody can check

D11's bind × token matrix decided from values, before anything is bound (design D11, docs/7 P5a): `Posture::of` takes a `SocketAddr` and the one flag the paragraph names, opens no socket, reads no environment and consults no clock, so all four cells are asserted on a machine with one interface — which is the whole reason the decision is a function rather than three lines inside a `bind` call, because deciding while binding leaves the two non-loopback cells testable only on a host whose network happens to cooperate, and that is the same as saying nothing checks them. The matrix is asserted twice over: one test per cell, each quoting the sentence of D11 it is about, and once as a *property* over nine addresses and both flag values, where token-less must happen exactly when the address is loopback and the flag was given — so a fifth cell added by accident fails here as well as in whichever cell test it belongs to. It also closes the hole an address that is loopback and does not say so: `Ipv6Addr::is_loopback` answers false for `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, the form a dual-stack listener sees for every IPv4 client, so the mapping is unwrapped before the question is asked, the whole of `127.0.0.0/8` is asked rather than `127.0.0.1`, all three wildcard binds are asserted **not** loopback including the mapped one, and the deprecated IPv4-compatible form is deliberately left where the kernel has it (note **N80**). What it does not establish is that anything reads the answer, or that the composition root decided a posture about the right address — the listener's row and `binary(wchd)`'s row below are those, and the suite says so in its own header rather than leaving it to be assumed

the per-run bearer token D11 asks for, treated as what it is — a secret this process mints, and therefore a secret this process can leak (design D11, docs/7 P5a). 32 bytes of `getrandom(2)` through rustix's `rand` feature rendered as 64 lowercase hex digits; two tokens minted in one process asserted to **differ**, which is the one property that makes it a secret rather than a password and the one a generator seeded from a pid or a start-of-process clock fails while passing everything else in the module; and the kernel-fill loop's property asserted where its branches cannot be, since the syscall is not a seam — over sixteen tokens no position may be a zero digit in all of them, which is what a partially filled buffer looks like. The confinement is asserted rather than asserted-about: the hand-written `Debug` does not contain the token and does say it is hiding something, and the same test reads the secret back through a rendering that is *not* the accessor it was read out of, so a `Token` that had quietly stopped yielding its secret fails here as well as in a browser. `verify` is driven at every shape a rewrite gets wrong first — a prefix, a suffix, an equal-length near miss, a case variant, and nothing at all — and the row is careful about what that is worth: **nothing in this suite can go red on the timing property itself**, because what a test can see is the answer and the claim is about the clock. The shape that argument stands on is `token-comparison-has-one-home.sh`'s row below, and the residual it leaves is note **N78**'s

the token gate's policy over values — which parts of a request may carry a credential, and what it means when more than one does (note **N74**, docs/7 P5a). The rule is that **every credential the request presents must verify, and it must present at least one**, and the three cases that tell it apart from the two gates this project refused to build are each asserted with the refused gate named in the failure message: a good header beside a bad query parameter, a repeated token parameter with the good copy first, and the same repeated with the good copy last — a first-wins gate serves the second, a last-wins gate serves the third, and the difference is reachable by anybody who can get one more parameter appended to a URL an operator is about to open. Two `Authorization` headers is the same rule again, because that is well-formed HTTP and `HeaderMap::get` would answer only the first of them. Beside those: an `Authorization` that is not a bearer credential counted as a credential that *failed* rather than as no credential at all, so a `Basic` header beside a good query parameter is refused by the rule rather than admitted down another path; the scheme compared case-insensitively as RFC 9110 requires and the token not, since it is hex this daemon minted lowercase; the grammar's extra spaces after the scheme allowed and a trailing one refused; a token parameter with no value at all treated as a credential that fails rather than as a request that presented nothing, which is what a URL truncated at its equals sign should meet; whole-name comparison, so a parameter that merely contains the name is somebody else's; and a percent-encoded token refused rather than decoded, so the secret has exactly one spelling. All of it takes a `HeaderMap` and a query string rather than a `Request`, so none of it needs a socket, a router or a runtime — the wire half is `binary(http)`'s row, and neither row is the other's rehearsal

the composition the listener performs, at the seams the integration suite cannot reach (docs/7 P5a). **A posture and a token that disagree are refused, in both directions**: a token-requiring posture with nothing minted is a gate with nothing to check, and a token-less posture with a token minted is a secret printed in a URL and never checked — both refused rather than resolved, because both resolutions are a socket onto a camera somebody did not mean to open, and with the two *agreeing* arrangements asserted to get a router, which is what makes the first two assertions about the disagreement rather than about a function that refuses everything. Then the one transformation between an HTTP path and an asset — the single leading slash stripped, the empty remainder read as the index page, and the name of that page owned by the asset crate rather than spelled here — with a parent-directory traversal, a doubled slash, a trailing slash and a path carrying no leading slash all answering nothing, not because a check catches a traversal but because the table of names is fixed at compile time and there is nothing to traverse (note **N77**). And `open` driven end to end on an ephemeral port for D11's "report the bound port": the URL carries the port the kernel gave and never the zero that was asked for, the token-less cell's URL carries no token parameter at all because an empty one reads as a token that failed to render, and both tests end by cancelling and joining rather than dropping the handle — which is exactly the detached task `Serving`'s `#[must_use]` message is about

docs/9's **Token enforcement** row, over a real TCP socket, a real axum server and a hand-written HTTP client — docs/7 P5a's "401-without/200-with" and "one test per matrix cell", which are one suite because the second is what stops the first being a claim about one cell. The credential every test presents is parsed out of `Serving::ready_to_open_url`, the line an operator copies, rather than read off the `Token` value: a build that published one secret and checked another would otherwise pass this whole suite, and that is the one bug a 401-without/200-with pair exists to be unable to survive. Both forms are driven, because they are two mechanisms a build can lose one at a time — the `Authorization` header, which is what code sends, and the query parameter, which is what a *navigation* can carry and therefore what an operator's first request is. All four cells are here: the two loopback ones through `http::open`, the function `wchd`'s composition root actually calls, and the two non-loopback ones through `http::serve` with a posture decided about `192.168.1.10:8080` and `0.0.0.0:8080` while the socket stays on loopback — the only way to reach them on a machine with one interface, and they establish that the gate is installed **because the posture said so** and nothing whatever about where the posture came from, which the suite's header states rather than leaves to be inferred. The refusal is asserted as three claims that do not imply one another — the status a client branches on, RFC 6750's challenge, and the body compared against the daemon's own constant, so a build that started answering with a stack trace or with the token fails here rather than in a review — and a path this build does not serve is asserted **401 while anonymous and 404 with the token**, which is the property that says the gate sits outside the router rather than inside it, and is why a stranger cannot map this daemon's surface by watching which paths answer differently (note **N75**). The token-less cell's claim is stronger than "a request with no token is served": no gate is installed at all, the URL the daemon published carries no token to leak, and the 404 still happens, so that cell removes the gate and not the router. Finally the printed URL is taken apart and **opened** rather than matched against a pattern, and the listener is stopped the way the daemon stops it, with the port asserted to refuse a connection afterwards

D11's "TCP is **opt-in**" at the surface where it is opt-in, and the half `crates/daemon/tests/http.rs` says out loud it cannot establish — that the composition root decides its posture from the right two values (docs/7 P5a). `--http` absent parses to `None`, which is neither a default address nor a disabled listener but the branch in `run` that opens no socket and mints no token: a flag that quietly acquired a `default_value` would put a TCP socket on every `wchd` on the machine while passing every other test in the file. `--http` alone takes D11's `127.0.0.1:0`, with the port asserted to be the kernel's to pick, and is asserted **not** to eat the flag that follows it, which is what an optional value would otherwise do to a command line. A host **name** is refused by the parser rather than resolved, because how far a bind reaches is what decides whether a token is required and a name with several addresses behind it is a name with several answers to that question. And `--http-insecure-loopback` is refused without `--http` — a flag that parses cleanly and does nothing is the second way an operator comes to believe in a listener that is not there — while being deliberately **not** refused off loopback, which is D11's fourth cell: the paragraph prescribes a token and a warning there, not a daemon that will not start, and `daemon::http::posture` is what makes the flag inert and says so in the warning

the client's files as bytes inside the binary that serves them (design §2.7's "no build step, no npm, no CDN (assets embed; external fetches would violate both the offline posture and the license inventory)", docs/7 P5a's "rust-embed asset serving skeleton"). **`debug-embed` is asserted rather than merely configured** (note **N77**): every embedded asset's bytes are `Cow::Borrowed`, which is a slice of the binary, and the assertion walks every asset rather than sampling one because the feature is per-build — without it a debug `wchd` reads its asset directory off the filesystem at the absolute path this crate was compiled from, which works on the machine that built it, serves nothing anywhere else, and means the daemon's whole HTTP suite exercises a *different mechanism* from the one a release binary ships. Every embedded asset is asserted to carry a content type, over a population the embed itself lists rather than one this suite wrote, and the count is asserted non-zero because a walk that found nothing is exactly how a crate that had stopped embedding its own directory would look; the four-entry table is then driven directly, fallback arm included, which the walk can never reach while every shipped asset is typed. `INDEX` — the one name the daemon spells — is asserted embedded and asserted to be HTML, because a rename that left the constant behind is a 404 at the root path, and the root path is the URL D11 asks an operator to open. What this crate does not do is turn bytes into a response: that is the daemon's law (design §2.10), and `dependency-walls.sh`'s row below is what keeps it there rather than a sentence in a header

the gate a surviving mutant produced, and the one criterion in this phase that exists because a *test* could not be written (note **N78**, AGENTS rule 1, design §2.10). Replacing `Token::verify`'s constant-time body with an equality on the exposed secret leaves every test in this workspace passing — the answer is identical for every input, and the only thing that changed is how long the daemon takes to say no — so the defect class is real, invisible to the suite, and gets no exemption from "every anticipated or discovered defect class becomes a lint, a CI job, or a test that can go red". This predicate cannot measure a clock, so it holds the four shape claims the timing argument stands on: the secret has **one reader**, and `expose_secret` outside `token.rs` appears only inside `#[cfg(test)]` — `gate.rs` naming it in product code is the defect spelled out one line before the comparison; the type implements no `PartialEq`, `Eq`, `Hash` or `Display` anywhere in the workspace, derived or hand-written; `Debug` is hand-written and names no field of the struct, with the field names read out of the declaration rather than typed into the predicate; and something still **calls** the comparison, because every claim above is true of a tree where the gate stopped checking the token. Every population it uses is derived — the daemon's directory from `cargo metadata`, the files from the tree walk, the fields from the declaration — and every name it treats as policy is asserted to exist first, so a rename or a move fails it rather than quietly emptying it. The row inherits its stated limit rather than restating it as a strength: this checks shape, an early `return false` written *inside* `verify` passes all four claims, and what defends that is the argument beside the code and the person reading the diff

docs/9 Part 2's **Web-fetch gate non-vacuity** row, commissioned at P5a by name and landed with the assets that made it assertable (design §2.7: external fetches "would violate both the offline posture and the license inventory"). Ten rules — a script tag with a scheme in its source, an off-origin stylesheet, a fetch and an ES import to another origin, a WebSocket to one, a CSS webfont — each quantify over the files the walk finds, so a walk that finds none makes all ten of them vacuously true, and **the greenest this gate could be was the state in which it was checking nothing at all**. Until `crates/web/assets/index.html` existed the emptiness was the honest answer and was printed as a named, counted skip; the skip is gone, and an asset directory that is empty — or missing, which reaches the same place, because a walk says nothing about what is not there — is now a failure. Anchors stay deliberately outside the rules: a link a user may click is not a subresource the page loads. What the criterion is worth is a function of the population it runs over, and that population is one file today, a skeleton page whose styles are inline for the reason note **N76** records — so this row grows with P5c's modules rather than being finished by P5a

the T6 wall P5a's new crate needed and design §2.8's list did not have (docs/7 P5a, design §2.10). `webcam-handler-web` links **neither** stack — no tokio, no axum, no hyper, no tower-http — and it is its own rule in the predicate rather than a name added to one of the existing lists, because the pure wall does not cover `tower-http` at all and the wire wall allows tokio for a reason (note N5) that has nothing to say about an asset crate. The crate's own manifest already turns `rust-embed`'s `axum-ex` integration down with this argument — "the axum one would give this crate its own axum and tokio edges, and serving is `webcam-handler-daemon`'s half of the seam" — and a manifest comment is an argument until something can go red on it.
